2609.11281.title: Bio-inspired Learning and Decision-Making with Probabilistic In-Memory Computing Hardware: Part 1
2609.11281.paper_summary: Learning and decision-making in animals are often modeled as Bayesian processes, where sensory evidence is integrated with prior beliefs to guide behavior in the face of uncertainty. But what are the inherent neural dynamics that give rise to this ability, and how could they be replicated in computing systems? This abstract discusses a biologically grounded framework in which noisy neural and synaptic dynamics perform inference and learning via stochastic sampling from an internal energy function, capturing uncertainty over latent states and model parameters through neural and synaptic variability, respectively. This enables approaches such as predictive coding networks to account for epistemic uncertainty via Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. Drawing a parallel between intrinsic noise in biological systems and electrical noise in emerging probabilistic analogue memory technologies, we highlight how analogue in-memory computing hardware naturally emerges as the solution for massively scalable and energy-efficient probabilistic inference.
2609.11281.paper_summary_zh: 學習和決策在動物中通常被建模為貝葉斯過程，其中感官證據與先前信念相結合，以指導在不確定性面前的行為。<lb/>但產生這種能力的內在神經動態是什麼？它們又如何在計算系統中被複製？<lb/>這篇摘要討論了一個生物學基礎的框架，在這個框架中，嘈雜的神經和突觸動態通過從內部能量函數的隨機抽樣來執行推理和學習，分別捕捉潛在狀態和模型參數的不確定性，通過神經和突觸變異性。<lb/>這使得像預測編碼網絡這樣的方法能夠通過馬爾可夫鏈蒙特卡羅抽樣來考慮認知不確定性。<lb/>通過將生物系統中的內在噪聲與新興的概率類比記憶技術中的電噪聲進行比較，我們強調了類比內存計算硬體如何自然地成為大規模可擴展和能源高效的概率推理的解決方案。
